description: An introduction to the chemistry laboratory, its rules and apparatus, hazard warning symbols, safe handling and heating techniques, fire prevention and control, filtration, and first aid.

mcq.questionText: A chemistry laboratory is best described as a place where:
mcq.explanation: A laboratory is a special room designed for carrying out scientific experiments safely. Exam Tip: The lab is built with safety features (fume cupboard, water, gas) specifically for experiments.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a correct laboratory rule?

options.text: Eating and drinking in the laboratory
Never eat, drink or taste anything in the laboratory

mcq.explanation: Chemicals may be poisonous, so no eating, drinking or tasting is allowed. Exam Tip: A, B and D are all dangerous behaviours.

mcq.questionText: The correct way to smell a gas or chemical in the laboratory is to:

options.text: Put your nose close and inhale deeply
Waft (fan) the vapour towards your nose with your hand
Heat it and inhale the fumes

mcq.explanation: The safe method is to gently fan (waft) a little vapour towards the nose. Exam Tip: Never inhale directly. Wafting brings only a small, safe amount of vapour.

mcq.questionText: Which apparatus is used to measure a specific volume of liquid accurately?
mcq.explanation: A measuring cylinder has a scale for accurate volume. Exam Tip: A beaker only estimates volume; use a measuring cylinder for accuracy.

mcq.questionText: The apparatus used for heating substances over a flame in the laboratory is the:
mcq.explanation: The Bunsen burner produces an adjustable flame using gas. Exam Tip: Its blue (roaring) flame is hottest; the yellow flame is cooler and dirty.

mcq.questionText: Which piece of apparatus is used to hold a hot test tube during heating?
mcq.explanation: A test-tube holder grips a hot tube safely at a distance. Exam Tip: Never hold hot apparatus with bare hands. Point the mouth away from people.

mcq.questionText: A warning sign showing a skull and crossbones on a chemical bottle means the chemical is:
mcq.explanation: The skull and crossbones means toxic/poisonous. Exam Tip: skull = toxic, flame = flammable, corrosive symbol = corrosive.

mcq.questionText: A hazard warning symbol showing a flame indicates that the substance is:
mcq.explanation: A flame warns that the substance can easily catch fire. Exam Tip: Flammable substances (ethanol, petrol) must be kept away from open flames.

mcq.questionText: The first thing you should do if a chemical splashes into your eye is to:

options.text: Wash the eye with plenty of clean water immediately
Close the eye and continue working

mcq.explanation: Immediate first aid is to rinse with plenty of clean running water. Exam Tip: For chemical splashes, the first action is always to wash with plenty of water. Rubbing spreads damage.

mcq.questionText: Which class of fire is caused by burning flammable liquids such as petrol and kerosene?
mcq.explanation: Flammable liquids (petrol, kerosene, oil) form Class B fires. Exam Tip: Class A = solids; Class B = flammable liquids; Class C = gases.

mcq.questionText: Which is the correct order of the three things needed for a fire to burn (the fire triangle)?
mcq.explanation: A fire needs fuel, oxygen and heat together. Exam Tip: Remove any ONE side of the fire triangle and the fire goes out.

mcq.questionText: A fire extinguisher puts out a fire mainly by:

options.text: Cutting off oxygen and/or cooling the fire

mcq.explanation: Extinguishers smother the fire (cut off oxygen) and/or cool it. Exam Tip: A blanket smothers (removes oxygen); water cools (removes heat).

mcq.questionText: Why should water NOT be used to put out an electrical fire?

options.text: Water conducts electricity and can cause electric shock
Water makes the fire bigger by adding fuel

mcq.explanation: Water conducts electricity, so using it risks electric shock. Exam Tip: Use a carbon dioxide or dry-powder extinguisher for electrical fires, never water.

mcq.questionText: The apparatus used to filter and separate a solid from a liquid is a funnel together with:
mcq.explanation: Filter paper in a funnel traps the solid while the liquid passes through. Exam Tip: Funnel + filter paper = filtration. Solid caught = residue; liquid through = filtrate.

mcq.questionText: When heating a liquid in a test tube, you should:

options.text: Point the mouth towards your friend
Point the mouth away from people and heat gently, shaking the tube
Hold it with your bare hand

mcq.explanation: Point the mouth away from everyone, heat gently and shake to spread the heat. Exam Tip: Never fill a heated tube more than one-third; always use a holder.

fib.questionText: A special room designed and equipped for carrying out scientific experiments is called a __________.
fib.explanation: A laboratory is the special room equipped for scientific experiments. Exam Tip: Write laboratory in full for marks.

fib.questionText: The apparatus commonly used as a source of heat in the chemistry laboratory is the __________.
fib.explanation: The Bunsen burner produces an adjustable gas flame used for heating. Exam Tip: Its hottest flame is the blue (non-luminous) flame.

fib.questionText: The hazard warning symbol of a __________ shows that a chemical is poisonous (toxic).
fib.explanation: The skull and crossbones is the recognised symbol for toxic chemicals. Exam Tip: Skull and crossbones = toxic/poisonous.

fib.questionText: The three things needed for a fire to start and continue burning are fuel, heat and __________.
fib.explanation: Oxygen is the third side of the fire triangle alongside fuel and heat. Exam Tip: Fuel + heat + oxygen = the fire triangle.

fib.questionText: The safe way to smell a chemical in the laboratory is by __________ the vapour towards the nose.
fib.explanation: Wafting brings only a small, safe amount of vapour towards the nose. Exam Tip: Never inhale directly over the container.

fib.questionText: In the laboratory, the equipment kept ready to give immediate treatment for minor injuries is the __________.
fib.explanation: A first aid kit provides immediate treatment for minor injuries. Exam Tip: A first aid kit holds bandages, cotton wool, antiseptic, plasters.

fib.questionText: Fires caused by burning solids such as wood and paper are classified as Class __________ fires.
fib.explanation: Burning solids like wood and paper are Class A fires. Exam Tip: Class A = solids; Class B = flammable liquids; Class C = gases.

fib.questionText: The laboratory apparatus used to hold a hot test tube while heating is a __________.
fib.explanation: A test-tube holder grips a hot tube safely at a distance. Exam Tip: Never grip a hot tube with bare fingers.

fib.questionText: The liquid that passes through the filter paper during filtration is called the __________.
fib.explanation: The liquid that passes through the filter paper is the filtrate. Exam Tip: Filtrate = liquid through; residue = solid on the paper.

fib.questionText: For an electrical fire, the correct type of extinguisher to use is a carbon dioxide or __________ extinguisher, not water.
fib.explanation: Carbon dioxide and dry-powder extinguishers are safe on electrical fires. Exam Tip: CO2 and dry-powder extinguishers are safe on electrical fires; water causes shock.

tf.questionText: Eating and drinking are allowed in the chemistry laboratory.
tf.explanation: Chemicals may be poisonous, so eating, drinking and tasting are never allowed. Exam Tip: No eating, drinking or tasting in the lab.

tf.questionText: A skull and crossbones symbol warns that a chemical is poisonous.
tf.explanation: The skull and crossbones is the recognised symbol for a toxic chemical. Exam Tip: Recognise hazard symbols on sight.

tf.questionText: You should taste chemicals to find out what they are.
tf.explanation: Tasting chemicals is dangerous because many are poisonous. Exam Tip: Never taste laboratory chemicals.

tf.questionText: A fire needs fuel, heat and oxygen in order to burn.
tf.explanation: These three together form the fire triangle needed for burning. Exam Tip: Firefighting removes any one side.

tf.questionText: Water is the best choice for putting out an electrical fire.
tf.explanation: Water conducts electricity and can cause an electric shock. Exam Tip: Use CO2 or dry powder on electrical fires, never water.

tf.questionText: When heating a substance in a test tube, the mouth of the tube should point away from people.
tf.explanation: Pointing the mouth away protects people if the contents spurt out. Exam Tip: Point away, heat gently, never fill more than one-third.

tf.questionText: A first aid kit is used to give immediate help for minor injuries.
tf.explanation: A first aid kit provides immediate treatment for minor injuries. Exam Tip: Wash chemical splashes with water; cool minor burns with cold water.

tf.questionText: The safe way to smell a gas is to inhale it deeply and directly.
tf.explanation: Direct deep inhaling is dangerous; the safe way is to waft the vapour towards the nose. Exam Tip: Direct deep inhaling is dangerous; wafting is safe.

tf.questionText: Flammable substances should be kept away from open flames.
tf.explanation: Flammable substances catch fire easily, so they must be kept away from flames. Exam Tip: Store flammable chemicals away from heat and flames.

tf.questionText: During filtration, the solid left on the filter paper is called the filtrate.
tf.explanation: The solid left on the paper is the residue; the filtrate is the liquid that passes through. Exam Tip: Residue = solid on the paper; filtrate = liquid through. The statement swaps them.

summary.correctAnswer: A special room designed and equipped for carrying out scientific experiments safely.
summary.explanation: It is fitted with safety features such as a fume cupboard, water and gas supply. Exam Tip: The lab is built specifically for safe experimenting.

summary.correctAnswer: Safety instructions such as never eating, drinking or tasting chemicals and not running during experiments.
summary.explanation: The rules exist to protect students from poisonous chemicals and accidents. Exam Tip: Most lab rules trace back to avoiding poisoning, burns or fire.

summary.correctAnswer: A hazard warning symbol meaning the chemical is poisonous (toxic).
summary.explanation: It warns you not to taste or inhale the chemical. Exam Tip: Skull = toxic; do not taste or inhale.

summary.correctAnswer: A hazard warning symbol meaning the substance is flammable and easily catches fire.
summary.explanation: Flammable substances such as ethanol and petrol must be kept from open flames. Exam Tip: Flame symbol = keep away from flames.

summary.correctAnswer: A hazard warning symbol, showing liquid burning a hand, meaning the substance can eat away skin and materials.
summary.explanation: You must avoid skin contact with corrosive chemicals such as strong acids. Exam Tip: Corrosive symbol = avoid skin contact.

summary.correctAnswer: The laboratory apparatus that produces an adjustable flame using gas, used as a source of heat.
summary.explanation: Its blue roaring flame is the hottest, while the yellow flame is cooler and dirty. Exam Tip: Use the blue flame for strong, clean heating.

summary.correctAnswer: The three things a fire needs to burn: fuel, oxygen and heat.
summary.explanation: Removing any one of the three sides puts the fire out. Exam Tip: Remove one side and the fire goes out.

summary.correctAnswer: Groups of fires by the burning material: Class A solids, Class B flammable liquids and Class C gases.
summary.explanation: Knowing the class helps you choose the correct extinguisher. Exam Tip: A = solids, B = liquids, C = gases.

summary.correctAnswer: Selecting the right extinguisher for the fire, for example carbon dioxide or dry powder for electrical fires and never water.
summary.explanation: The extinguisher works by cutting off oxygen and/or cooling the fire. Exam Tip: Never use water on electrical or liquid fires.

summary.correctAnswer: Immediate treatment given for minor injuries, such as washing a chemical splash with plenty of clean water.
summary.explanation: A first aid kit holds bandages, cotton wool, antiseptic and plasters. Exam Tip: For splashes, wash with plenty of water first.

hoq.questionText: During an experiment, a small fire starts on the bench when some kerosene catches alight. A student wants to put it out. Which action is correct, and why?

options.text: Pour water on it, because water cools everything
Cover it with a fire blanket or use a suitable extinguisher, because this cuts off the oxygen supply
Blow on it hard, because air puts out fire
Add more kerosene to control it

hoq.explanation: Burning kerosene is a Class B fire. Water can spread a liquid fire, so the safe method is to remove oxygen by smothering with a blanket or extinguisher. Exam Tip: For burning liquids never use water. Blowing adds oxygen; adding fuel is wrong.

hoq.questionText: A student sees three bottles with these hazard symbols: Bottle 1 a flame; Bottle 2 a skull and crossbones; Bottle 3 a symbol showing liquid burning a hand. How should the student treat each bottle?

options.text: 1 keep from flames, 2 do not taste/inhale, 3 avoid skin contact
1 drink freely, 2 taste it, 3 rub on skin
1 heat strongly, 2 smell deeply, 3 pour on hands
All three are safe to handle without care

hoq.explanation: Bottle 1 (flame) is flammable, so keep it from flames; Bottle 2 (skull) is toxic, so do not taste or inhale; Bottle 3 (liquid on hand) is corrosive, so avoid skin contact. Exam Tip: Each hazard symbol prescribes a specific precaution.

hoq.questionText: A student accidentally spills a strong acid on the bench and a little splashes onto her hand. Arrange the CORRECT sequence of actions: (i) Report to the teacher (ii) Wash the hand with plenty of running water (iii) Wipe up the spilled acid safely as directed.

options.text: (ii) then (iii) then (i) only if there is time

hoq.explanation: The most urgent danger is acid on the skin, so wash the hand with plenty of running water first (ii), then report to the teacher (i), who directs safe cleaning of the spill (iii). Exam Tip: Safety priority is PEOPLE first, then report, then clean up. Never delay washing the skin.
